title: Sizing a Liquidity strategy
passages: A Liquidity strategy is sized to cover two to five years of planned spending, held in instruments that do not require selling risk assets during a drawdown.
Where a Liquidity strategy is unfunded, new cash inflows are the lowest-cost source of funding because no position has to be sold.

title: Treasury ladder, 0 to 3 years
passages: Laddered US Treasuries mature on a schedule matched to planned withdrawals. Market value can move before maturity; held to maturity, principal is returned at par.

title: Managing single-name concentration
passages: Concentration above a household's policy threshold can be reduced through staged sales under an existing trading plan, an exchange fund, or hedging, each with different tax and liquidity costs.
Staged sales that realise short-term gains carry a higher tax cost than sales of lots held longer than one year.

title: Exchange fund, 7-year lockup
passages: Contributors receive units in a diversified partnership. A seven-year holding period applies before a diversified basket may be distributed.

title: Municipal ladder, 1 to 7 years
passages: A municipal ladder provides tax-exempt income with scheduled maturities for high-bracket households.

title: Non-US pooled funds held by US taxpayers
passages: Holdings in non-US pooled funds may be classified as PFICs for US taxpayers, with punitive default tax treatment unless an election is made.

title: Account review and documentation procedure
passages: Unsigned account documents older than 14 days are escalated to the branch supervisor.
Client information is refreshed on a 36-month cycle or on a material life event.

title: Standard client communication disclosure
passages: This note describes options for discussion. It is not a projection of future performance and not a recommendation until reviewed with your advisor.
